accepted_facts.text: The normalizer is local and bounded.
Only the owner may adopt a repair proposal.
Acceptance requires an independent validator result.
V-001 is explained by inline-hash truncation in profile_loader.py; the available local evidence does not indicate a separate value-normalization cause.
The observed loss of the inline hash is localized to the unconditional split at # in normalize_profile; the existing quoted-value stripping remains separate and applicable.
The local policy resolves U-001 in favor of retaining an inline # as data, so the current implementation conflicts with policy before independent validation can pass.

The Python 3.12 configparser documentation states that inline comments are disabled by default, while # and ; are whole-line comment prefixes; it also warns that enabling inline comments prevents those characters from being used in values.

The bounded research supports narrowing U-002 to unconditional inline-hash truncation during parsing/normalization; no separate quoted-value normalization cause is indicated by the current local evidence.

In Python 3.12 configparser, inline_comment_prefixes defaults to None, so inline comments are disabled by default; # and ; remain whole-line comment prefixes, and enabling inline comments can prevent those characters from being used in values.
normalize_profile unconditionally applies line.split("#", 1) before key/value parsing, which changes the fixture title from Alpha # tag to Alpha and directly matches V-001.
The narrow repair boundary is the inline-hash truncation step; existing quoted-value stripping should remain unchanged.

V-002 is a key canonicalization mismatch in the repaired projection: key.strip() preserves Title, while the independent validator expects the canonical key title; this is separate from the already addressed inline-hash truncation.

The available current evidence establishes a validation gap, not acceptance: validator-report-post-repair.json reports independent false and acceptance_evidence false, while independent-validator.py defines the required canonical result.
The alternate key-canonicalization repair is owner-adopted for this continuation and must be treated as adopted, but G6 has not executed it.

active_hypothesis.statement: The remaining V-002 failure is caused by missing key canonicalization; the owner-adopted narrow repair should lowercase the normalized key while preserving inline # data and existing quoted-value normalization.

invalidated_hypotheses.reason: The initially plausible route of treating every inline # as a comment was rejected by local policy and source-bound research.
